steps.en: Install the controller into kube-system with the Helm chart
steps.zh: 用 Helm chart 把控制器装进 kube-system

steps.en: Declare which strategies to run in a DeschedulerPolicy
steps.zh: 在 DeschedulerPolicy 里声明要跑哪些策略

steps.en: Computes every node's utilization from pod requests and finds the over- and under-utilized ones
steps.zh: 按 Pod 的 requests 算出各节点利用率，找出过热与空闲的节点

steps.en: Filters candidates through its pod protections, then evicts the rest through the Eviction API
steps.zh: 按 Pod 保护规则过滤候选，其余走 Eviction API 驱逐

steps.en: Their controllers recreate the evicted pods and kube-scheduler places them elsewhere
steps.zh: 被驱逐的 Pod 由控制器重建，kube-scheduler 另择节点放置

value.en: A cluster that drifts back toward balance on a schedule — you no longer hand-pick pods to drain node by node
value.zh: 集群会按期自己漂回均衡——不用你再逐个节点手动挑 Pod 去腾挪

sources: README → Quick Start ("The descheduler can be run as a `Job`, `CronJob`, or `Deployment` inside of a k8s cluster... The descheduler pod is run as a critical pod in the `kube-system` namespace to avoid being evicted by itself or by the kubelet.")

README → Install Using Helm ("Starting with release v0.18.0 there is an official helm chart that can be used to install the descheduler.") and charts/descheduler/README.md (`helm repo add descheduler https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/descheduler/`; `helm install my-release --namespace kube-system descheduler/descheduler`; "To preview what changes descheduler would make without actually going forward with the changes, you can install descheduler in dry run mode by providing the flag `--set cmdOptions.dry-run=true`")
README → Install Using Kustomize (`kustomize build 'github.com/kubernetes-sigs/descheduler/kubernetes/cronjob?ref=release-1.34' | kubectl apply -f -`)

README → Example policy (`apiVersion: "descheduler/v1alpha2"`, `kind: "DeschedulerPolicy"`, `profiles:` → `pluginConfig: - name: "DefaultEvictor"` with `podProtections` and `nodeFit`, then `plugins:` with `deschedule:`/`balance:` `enabled:` lists)

README → LowNodeUtilization ("evicts pods from `overutilized nodes` (those with usage above `targetThresholds`) to `underutilized nodes`"; "By default node resource consumption is determined by the requests and limits of pods, not actual usage... consistent with the kube-scheduler")

README → Pod Evictions → Pod Disruption Budget (PDB), and the strategy table listing RemoveDuplicates / LowNodeUtilization / HighNodeUtilization as `Balance` plugins and RemovePodsViolating* / PodLifeTime / RemoveFailedPods as `Deschedule` plugins
